card.title: Indeterminate forms — seven signals, four tools

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Limits formalise approach (ε–δ: |f(x)−L| < ε whenever 0 < |x−a| < δ — the point itself excluded). Seven indeterminate forms (0/0, ∞/∞, 0·∞, ∞−∞, 1^∞, 0^0, ∞^0) signal substitution's failure, each with its rewrite tool: factorise, rationalise, divide by highest power, or deploy standard limits (sinx/x → 1, (1+1/n)^n → e). Continuity demands limit = value (no jumps/holes); differentiability demands continuity plus smoothness (no corners) — continuous need not be differentiable.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: forms: 0/0 · ∞/∞ · 0·∞ · ∞−∞ · 1^∞ · 0^0 · ∞^0  ·  tools: factor/cancel · conjugate · ÷highest power · sinx/x→1 · (1+x)^(1/x)→e  ·  continuous at a: lim = f(a) · differentiable ⟹ continuous (converse false: |x| at 0)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Two-sided limits need matching one-sided equals. Standard trig limits need radian measure. Continuity checks all three: f(a) defined, limit exists, equality holds. Differentiability additionally needs the left/right derivative match.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: |x| at 0: continuous (limit 0 = value) but cornered — left derivative −1, right +1, so NOT differentiable (the canonical counterexample). 1^∞ forms (like (1+1/n)^n) resolve via logarithms to e-powers. Removable holes factor away; jumps and asymptotes never resolve.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: lim(x→0)(sin 3x)/x: scale to the standard form → 3·sin(3x)/(3x) → 3×1 = 3. Continuity drill: f(x) = (x²−4)/(x−2) for x≠2 with f(2) = 5 — limit is 4 ≠ 5, so discontinuous (removable); reset f(2) = 4 to heal it.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: L'Hôpital-style shortcuts sit outside this syllabus's toolkit — rewrite, don't differentiate, the limit away. Graphical intuition misleads on wild oscillation (sin(1/x) near 0). Continuity at a point says nothing about intervals (uniform continuity is stronger).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Why 0<|x−a| matters: excluding the point lets limits exist where functions don't (holes have limits). Differentiable⟹continuous proof: f(x)−f(a) = [f(x)−f(a)]/(x−a)·(x−a) → f′(a)·0 = 0. Contrapositive powers the |x| verdict: corner ⇒ not differentiable, while continuity holds separately.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Form radar: 0/0 → factor/conjugate · ∞/∞ → divide by highest power · exponential forms → take ln. Continuity checklist: defined? limit? equal? Differentiability: continuity first, then corner-hunt.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: seven forms with one rewrite tool each; standard-limit evaluations (trig + exponential); continuity verdicts with healing; |x|-style differentiability counterexample.
